strengths: The paper is well-organized and clearly written.
The proposed method is technically sound.
The collected dataset for developing and evaluating the proposed method is relatively large-scale.
The paper presents the applied problem well.
weaknesses: The novelty of this work is limited from a methodological perspective.

Additionally, there is a lack of comprehensive comparisons with other studies.
The novelty of this work is limited.

The evaluation of this work is insufficient.

The figures quality needs improve.
I find that this paper seems to have been generated by a scientific LLM agent. There are many inconsistencies in citations and formatting that appear to be hallucinations.

The paper contains inaccurate statistics and citations in the Introduction, such as claiming kidney cancer affects over 10% of the global population and is projected to rise from the tenth leading cause of death in 2024.
The paper reports incorrect prevalence figures for nephrolithiasis (17% instead of the correct 12%).
The citation for CT scan effectiveness is inaccurate and does not support the claimed statement.
The related work section cites an inappropriate reference (Tan & Le, 2020) for CNNs and uses unnatural phrasing like "grid-patterned dataset".
The manuscript includes odd phrasing that resembles AI-generated text, such as repeated "I..... I..... I....." statements.
The attribution of transfer learning to Zhuang et al., 2020 is misleading, as the technique predates that work.
The citation of TensorFlow (Tan & Le, 2021; He et al., 2016; Khan et al., 2020) is incorrect and unrelated.
The citation pairing batch normalization with an irrelevant SimCLR paper (Chen et al., 2020) is erroneous.
Reporting 100% accuracy without detailed analysis is suspicious and unlikely in realistic machine learning tasks.
The transformation of a multi-class classification dataset into binary classes is unexplained and offers no clear benefit.
Prior work in 2023 compared similar models on the same Kaggle dataset, making this paper's contributions negligible.
The paper has virtually no novelty and doesn't really seem like a research paper.
There are no methodological contributions.
The experiment and the results are not extensive enough nor evaluated properly.
The paper only applies two existing neural networks to an open dataset and labels the highest mean performing model as the winner.
All steps of the ML pipeline would need improvement, such as proper hyper-parameter search.
More methods should be evaluated on more datasets.
Confidence intervals, standard errors, or statistical tests should be performed.
The paper does not seem suitable for ICLR and would be more appropriate for a journal for renal disease studies.
